research_mode: official ONS, Home Office and Police.uk sources only; repeat-victimisation, sensitive self-completion, domestic-abuse measure transitions, outcome definitions and Police.uk identity or missing-location semantics; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: CSEW self-completion topic scope
verified_claims: self-completion modules cover domestic abuse
they also cover sexual assault and stalking
other modules include drug use drinking gangs and personal security
limitations: module availability can vary by survey edition
different topics can use different denominators

sources.name: Self-completion confidentiality rationale
verified_claims: sensitive questions are completed privately on a tablet
the design is intended to increase respondent comfort
privacy and confidentiality are central reasons for self-completion
limitations: privacy design does not eliminate under-reporting
mode and safeguarding rules must be retained

sources.name: Domestic-abuse split-sample module trade-off
verified_claims: the domestic-abuse trial used a split sample
half received existing questions and half received new questions
respondents receiving new questions did not receive the existing sexual-assault and stalking questions in that module space
limitations: trial arms have different available variables
combined estimates require explicit questionnaire routing

sources.name: New domestic-abuse reference periods
verified_claims: new questions were designed for estimates since age 16
they were also designed for last-year estimates
reference periods are separately defined
limitations: lifetime and last-year measures are not interchangeable
recall and exposure periods differ

sources.name: New domestic-abuse questionnaire structure
verified_claims: the questionnaire has separate partner and family sections
each section asks about abusive behaviours
the design also asks about impacts of those behaviours
limitations: behaviour and impact measures answer different questions
question wording version must be retained

sources.name: Domestic-abuse self-completion age coverage change
verified_claims: face-to-face CSEW collection resumed on 4 October 2021
the upper age limit for domestic-abuse sexual-assault and stalking self-completion modules was removed
coverage after the change differs from earlier age-limited series
limitations: age-coverage change creates comparability considerations
post-resumption estimates also depend on interview-month coverage

sources.name: Domestic-abuse multi-source comparison rule
verified_claims: the domestic-abuse release combines several data sources
sources use different timescales and reference periods
the datasets do not all count the same thing and cannot be directly compared
limitations: a combined narrative is not a merged metric
source-specific units and populations must remain visible

sources.name: Year ending March 2022 domestic-abuse caution
verified_claims: year ending March 2022 estimates used six months of face-to-face interviews
the estimates were not accredited official statistics
ONS instructs users to interpret them with caution
limitations: the six-month estimate is not equivalent to a normal 12-month collection
designation must be preserved

sources.name: Domestic-abuse survey-error exclusion
verified_claims: year ending March 2023 estimates used eight months of interviews
October 2022 to January 2023 data were excluded
an error in the survey caused missing data for some respondents
limitations: partial-year estimates require explicit month coverage
the error affects comparability and precision

sources.name: Domestic-abuse question transition timetable
verified_claims: new questions entered a split-sample trial from April 2023
the trial concluded in March 2025
from April 2025 the full sample received the new questions
limitations: trial and full-sample phases require different metadata
transition timing can affect annual estimates
